_README: The SOURCE OF TRUTH for this agent's `capabilities.output_contract`.
Compile it with the `build_output_contract` MCP tool, or
output; this file is the input. `tests/equity_analyst_contract.rs`
asserts the two agree, so the card cannot be edited away from the
declaration that produced it — which is the drift every generated
artefact in this repo has eventually suffered.
Five sourced blocks and one judgement block expand to 12 schema
properties, 12 grounding entries and 5 narrowed provenance enums. The
expansion is in src/contract_sketch.rs and is the same for every agent,
which is the point: what is written here is only what needed deciding.
Read docs/guides/AGENT_CONTRACT_AUTHORING.md for the statuses, and
docs/DESIGN_typed_output_contracts.md for why this file exists.
title: Equity evidence
description: Evidence supporting one driver of a Fermi forecast, from a member of the research orchestra. The retrieved blocks are Financial Modeling Prep responses; `assessment` is the agent's own judgement over them and is stamped `model_inference` for exactly that reason. The split is the product: a coordinator weighting five members' multipliers can tell a retrieved multiple from a reasoned one, which is the distinction the delegation envelope existed to carry and had nothing typed to carry it over.

calibration.note: The agent's contribution resolves when the forecast it fed does. `assessment.multiplier_p50` is the scoreable quantity; the sourced blocks are inputs and are not scored, because a correctly retrieved P/E that led to a wrong multiplier is a reasoning failure and must not be charged to the retrieval.

blocks.name: profile
blocks.description: Who the issuer is and what the market currently pays for it.

source.response_field: symbol, companyName, sector, industry, price, marketCap, beta

blocks.why: FMP's /stable/profile returns every field of this block for a resolved ticker, or an empty array for a symbol it does not carry. Those are the only two outcomes, which is why the stamp admits exactly two verdicts. Note what is NOT here: nothing in this block is an opinion, so a null means the lookup failed rather than that the agent declined to guess.

blocks.name: valuation_multiples
blocks.description: What the market pays per unit of earnings, book and sales.

source.response_field: priceToEarningsRatio, priceToBookRatio, priceToSalesRatio, dividendYield for the requested period

blocks.why: FMP computes these ratios server-side, so the agent is reading them rather than deriving them from statements it also fetched. That matters for this contract specifically: a multiple the model divided out itself would be a judgement wearing a retrieval's clothes, and would belong under `assessment` instead.

period.description: Which reporting period was requested. Null when no ratio row came back at all.

blocks.name: intrinsic_value
blocks.description: FMP's own DCF estimate, beside the price on the same date.

source.response_field: dcf and stockPrice, both as returned on the same date

blocks.why: Both numbers come from the endpoint, and only those two. The implied upside is deliberately absent from this block even though it is one subtraction away: the moment the agent computes it the value stops being retrieved, and a field that is arithmetic over a vendor model is a judgement about that model. It lives under `assessment`, where the stamp says so.

blocks.name: fundamentals
blocks.description: Returns on capital, cash generation and leverage.
blocks.why: Coverage is partial rather than complete, and the distinction is load-bearing. /stable/key-metrics answers for the issuer, but individual members of this block are absent for whole classes of filer — free cash flow yield for a pre-revenue biotech, return on invested capital for a financial. That is not the tool having nothing for the symbol; it is the tool answering and the field having no source, which is a third verdict and is why this stamp admits `unavailable_no_tool_source` while `profile`'s does not.

blocks.name: analyst_consensus
blocks.description: Forward Wall Street estimates and how many analysts stand behind them.

source.response_field: date, revenueAvg, epsAvg, epsLow, epsHigh, numAnalystsEps

blocks.why: Forward estimates, retrieved rather than modelled. `analyst_count` is in the block on purpose: a consensus of two is a different object from a consensus of thirty, and without the count a downstream coordinator weights them identically. Uncovered symbols come back as an empty array, which is `tool_no_match` and honestly says the street is silent rather than that the street is neutral.

blocks.name: assessment
blocks.description: The agent's own judgement, and the only block a Fermi coordinator scores.

source.from: the retrieved profile, valuation_multiples, intrinsic_value, fundamentals and analyst_consensus blocks, weighed against the sector base rates in capabilities.fermi_contract.seed_facts

blocks.why: The load-bearing entry. Every number here is a judgement over the blocks above and can never be `tool_verified` however good those inputs were — two runs over one set of FMP responses may legitimately disagree about a multiplier, which is precisely what makes it not a retrieval. Stamped `model_inference` as a constant rather than an enum so no run can present a reasoned multiplier as a looked-up one. This is the field the Brier score in `calibration` eventually settles.

direction.description: `indeterminate` is a real answer, not a failure: with no DCF and no consensus there is nothing to be directional about, and a forced call there is noise a coordinator cannot distinguish from signal.

multiplier_p50.description: Multiplier on the Fermi driver base rate, NOT a probability. 1.0 means the evidence agrees with the base rate. capabilities.fermi_contract.multiplier_range bounds it to [0.1, 3.0]; the bound is stated here rather than as JSON Schema `minimum` because src/schema_validate.rs cannot evaluate `minimum`, and a schema carrying a keyword the validator skips reports the whole document `unverified_unsupported_schema` at the delegation hop — declaring more in exchange for verifying nothing.

multiplier_p5.description: Low end of the multiplier interval. Same [0.1, 3.0] bound and the same reason it is prose.

multiplier_p95.description: High end of the multiplier interval. Same [0.1, 3.0] bound and the same reason it is prose.

confidence.description: 0.0 to 1.0. Should fall when the sourced blocks came back thin — a confident multiplier over four nulls is the shape this contract exists to make visible.

key_findings.description: CEP findings, each prefixed with one of the labels in capabilities.fermi_contract.finding_labels: [BASE RATE], [VALUATION], [EARNINGS], [SECTOR], [MULTIPLIER]. The [MULTIPLIER] finding must be last and must restate p50/p5/p95, so the orchestra's existing text parser keeps working against a document that is now also typed.

blocks.name: summary
blocks.why: Prose for a human reading the forecast, and the field with the least protection: it is the one place a number the sourced blocks could not supply can reappear as a sentence. It must assert nothing the blocks above cannot support, and grounding_trust scans it for exactly that. It carries no provenance stamp because a retrieval verdict about a paragraph is a category error.
